_about: How sure a verdict is, as percents (agentcake/detect/confidence.py, plan step S3.7, decision D36): the chance each layer's evidence gives, combined by adding log-likelihood ratios as if humans and agents were equally common, each percent held inside clamp. agentcake eval checks them against sessions with known answers (its calibration table: per bin of predicted chance, the actual share; and the Brier score).

behaviour._about: The isotonic map from the behaviour score (the mean log-odds of the behaviour model's smoothed segment scores, each held inside -score_limit..score_limit) to the chance that an agent acted, both classes weighted alike, each block shrunk towards even by eval.json calibration.prior_count sessions of each class. blocks: [upper score, chance], in order; a score above the last upper bound takes the last chance. Fitted by the maintainers' calibration script on the sessions with known answers (the fit's data sets and date in fitted); agentcake eval refits it without each data set to check it held out.
behaviour.fitted: 2026-11-13: lab 26 agents and 0 people, recordings 0 agents and 11 people, recorded 32 agents and 0 people, selfcollect 10 agents and 0 people, public_humans 0 agents and 629 people, posthog 50 agents and 16 people

layers._about: Declared, not fitted (few people in our data show any of these, so no fit is possible yet): the chance of what the layer names (an agent, or a bot for a listed bot's name) when it found it. verified: a name a signature or published addresses confirm, and a verified signature; impersonation: a name a check proved false (an automation lying about what it is); self_reported: a name nothing confirms; env_hard: a hard automation or spoofing trace (never seen on people: 0 of our 11 clean recordings, botscent 0 of 44 to 90); env_counted: soft traces that count with another one; env_soft_alone: soft traces alone, which a person's own extensions can leave; typing_cadence: the session's typing ends at bot (agentcake/detect/cadence.py), added to the behaviour layer's own chance: 7 of the lab's 14 agents that typed 20 keys end at bot and 0 of 416 people (the recorder's 8 and the CMU keystroke benchmark's 408 sittings), a chance of 0.986 at the people's 95% upper bound, declared lower because those people typed a password, not free text.
